blocking.section: Concept mapping / KrakenD path entries and their targets; Migration gaps / Features that arrive after the importer
blocking.issue: The document gives two different fidelities for KrakenD EE streaming (SSE). The research says KrakenD configures SSE with no namespace: `output_encoding: no-op` on the endpoint, `encoding: no-op` on the backend and a long `timeout`. The document grades that exact shape `exact` with 'bytes stream unchanged'. Yet it lists 'SSE streaming' among the Planned (M3) features that 'import as `manual` (rule 4)'. The Data plane also tags SSE `text/event-stream` flushing Planned (M3), and Multi-protocol says a plain reverse proxy flushes `text/event-stream` only 'per read' before M3. So at the M2 importer release, a streaming endpoint that imports as `exact` does not deliver events the way KrakenD does, and the report says nothing about it.
blocking.evidence: Line 133: "| endpoint `output_encoding: no-op` | `Route` with plain `upstreams`; bytes stream unchanged | `exact` | Proxy-only in KrakenD"; line 148: "| backend `encoding: no-op` | Plain `upstreams` | `exact` |"; line 848: "Items whose target postdates the importer, Planned (M2), import as `manual` (rule 4)"; line 853: "| gRPC server and client, direct WebSockets, multiplexer, SSE streaming | `match.grpc`, `grpc` and `websocket` Upstreams, `onChunk` | Planned (M3) |". Research krakend-config-model.md: "`sse` | There is no namespace. EE streaming/SSE (since v2.12) is configured with `output_encoding: \"no-op\"` on the endpoint, `encoding: \"no-op\"` on the backend, and a long `timeout`". Data plane: "| SSE | `text/event-stream` response | `http.ResponseController` flushing | Planned (M3) |". Multi-protocol: "HTTP reverse proxy; `text/event-stream` flushes per read | Planned (M1); SSE flushing Planned (M3)". Parity matrix: "| Streaming and Server-Sent Events (SSE) | No | Yes | Planned (M3) |".
blocking.fix: In the `output_encoding: no-op` row (line 133), add this note: 'a no-op endpoint whose backends are all `encoding: no-op` is KrakenD's streaming configuration; before M3 the importer adds one `approximate` item per such Route, because `text/event-stream` flushes per read, not per event, until SSE, Planned (M3) ([Data plane](../architecture/03-data-plane.md))'. On line 853, replace 'SSE streaming' with 'SSE per-event flushing and `onChunk` Policies', and state that KrakenD streaming Routes import `approximate` through the no-op rows, not `manual`. Rule 4 still holds, because the reverse-proxy target exists from Planned (M1).

blocking.issue: This row grades the whole namespace `equivalent`, which breaks the document's own rules 4 and 7. First, `proxy_address` has no Ruralz field. It waits for OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-6 and is Planned (M5), so under rule 4 it must be `manual`. Second, the row claims equivalence only for `no_redirect: true`. For `no_redirect: false`, KrakenD follows the redirect and Ruralz returns the 3xx to the client, which is a different observable contract from the `equivalent` definition. Third, the research lists `send_body_on_redirect`, and the row does not map it. An operator reading `equivalent` would expect no action on a backend that relies on an egress proxy.
blocking.evidence: Line 230: "| `backend/http/client` | B | `client_tls` to `Upstream.spec.tls`; `no_redirect: true` is the Ruralz default, since 3xx responses pass through | `equivalent` | `proxy_address` per OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-6, Planned (M5)"; rule 4 (line 474): "Items whose target is not in the running release are `manual`."; rule 7 (line 477): "a missing value is reported rather than assumed"; line 463: "`equivalent` | Same routing, allow or deny decisions, status and payload semantics". Research: "`backend/http/client` | B | CE subset since v2.11 (`send_body_on_redirect`). EE adds `client_tls`, `no_redirect`, `proxy_address`". Parity matrix OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-6: "Where does an `Upstream` declare an egress HTTP proxy ... Yes, for the M5 intermediary web proxy row".
blocking.fix: Change the Fidelity cell to: '`equivalent` for `client_tls` and `no_redirect: true`; `approximate` for `no_redirect: false`, since Ruralz passes the 3xx to the client (OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-13); `manual` for `proxy_address` (rule 4, OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-6) and `send_body_on_redirect`'.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 19 claims the document maps "every `extra_config` namespace of the v2.13 schema", while line 173 more carefully claims "every v2.13 namespace the research records". Use the second wording in the Summary so the claim does not exceed the research.
Line 745 says shadow Nodes "never join the serving pool". Pack section 2 lists 'pool' as a never-write alias for Cluster. Write "never receive client traffic from the load balancer" instead.

non_blocking.section: Cutover runbook / Stages 4 and 5; Concept mapping / `router` row
non_blocking.suggestion: The `router` row maps `disable_access_log` and `logger_skip_paths` to Gateway `telemetry.accessLog.when`. Stage 4 needs `when` unset for pairing and per-Route `gateway_duration` baselines, and the rollback trigger reads serving Nodes' access logs. Add to Stage 1: during cutover, leave `telemetry.accessLog.when` unset in the Bundle, or restrict it only in ways that keep every request of watched Routes. Note also that changing it changes the Revision digest that Stages 3 and 5 check.

Line 478 says "an unresolved URL keeps Nodes not ready (RZ-CFG-026)". The Configuration model says the Node rejects the Revision and keeps serving its active Revision; only a Node without one stays not ready. Say: 'a Node that cannot resolve it rejects the Revision (RZ-CFG-026); a cold Node stays not ready'.

non_blocking.section: Plugin migration / Lua to CEL or WASM Plugins; Go plugins table
non_blocking.suggestion: The WASM Host Function table limits `request_body_read` and `request_body_replace` to `onRequestBody`, and `response_body_read` and `response_body_replace` to `onUpstreamResponseBody`. That rules out two Plugin targets. First, a `modifier/lua-proxy` `post` body rewrite at Route scope in `onResponse` (line 662, after the aggregate merge). Second, a backend-level request body modifier as an Upstream-scoped Plugin in `onUpstreamRequest` (lines 566 and 663). For those rows, name `transform.response` or `transform.request` as the only body target, or add an Open question.

The research lists `propagate_role` at service level, but the document does not map it. Map it to a Route `headers` Policy whose `request.set[].valueExpression` reads `consumer.tags`, or grade it `manual`.

non_blocking.suggestion: Line 275 grades only `GET` and `HEAD`. Add '`approximate` for methods with a body (OQ-migration-from-krakend-16)', as line 144 does for `url_pattern` rewrites.

Line 199 maps a backend-scope cache to a "Route `cache` Policy" without saying which Routes get it. State 'on every Route reaching the `Upstream`', as the `governance/quota` and `qos/ratelimit/proxy` rows do, and note that an aggregate Route then caches the merged response, not one backend call.

non_blocking.section: Import tool fidelity levels / SM-8 paragraph
non_blocking.suggestion: Line 467 says "every import holds forwarding items". The word 'holds' collides with the hold term of rule 2, and forwarding items carry no hold, so write 'has'. Also, while every import has a `manual` forwarding item, the proposed SM-8 definition scores 0% of the corpus. Say this explicitly in OQ-migration-from-krakend-10 so that the M2 exit risk is visible.

Step 3 compares the Node's active digest with the one `ruralz bundle build` printed. The Configuration model says a file-mode Cluster with more than one Node SHOULD load rendered Bundles or OCI Revisions. State that Nodes load the rendered Bundle or pull the pushed Revision by digest, so that the comparison holds.
Line 64 cites ADR-0003 for 'Content-addressed, verified by digest'. Digest verification belongs to pack section 8.1 and ADR-0017, so cite those, and keep ADR-0003 for the configuration format.

ac_results.ac: Concept mapping maps every top-level KrakenD configuration key and at least 20 extra_config namespaces to Ruralz kinds and Policies (KrakenD endpoint to Route, backend to Upstream, extra_config namespaces to Policies).
ac_results.note: All 36 root properties are mapped (lines 97-123), and 86 namespace rows are mapped (lines 177-262). The `backend/http/client` row is graded against the document's own rules (L2-2).

ac_results.ac: Import tool fidelity levels defines the fidelity levels reported by ruralz bundle import krakend (Planned (M2)) and what each guarantees.
ac_results.note: The four levels have guarantees, importer actions and operator actions. Eight rules, the report, annotation and exit statuses are consistent with the CLI exit codes. The `exact` guarantee now excludes client parameter forwarding.

ac_results.ac: Plugin migration covers both paths: Go plugins to WASM Plugins (TinyGo) or built-in Filters, and Lua to CEL or WASM Plugins.
ac_results.note: Both paths are covered, with an accessor-to-Host Function table and a Lua layer and use-case mapping. Two Plugin body targets conflict with Host Function Phases (non-blocking).

ac_results.ac: Cutover runbook gives ordered steps for shadow traffic and side-by-side cutover, including rollback.
ac_results.note: Stages 0-6 each have ordered steps, followed by a rollback trigger table and a gate summary. SM-4 is no longer used as a production gate. `ruralz test run` now passes `CASES`.

ac_results.ac: Migration gaps is consistent with the Not planned rows of docs/comparison/01-krakend-ee-parity-matrix.md.
ac_results.note: The 13 Not planned features, 3 of them EE-only, match the matrix. All 17 partial-parity rows are now covered, and OQ-krakend-ee-parity-matrix-4 is cited.
